claims.explanation: TAK-715 is a p38 MAPK inhibitor that also cross-reacts with casein kinase 1δ/ε (CSNK1D/E), inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Selectivity may arise from dependence on p38 MAPK or Wnt/β-catenin signaling for survival, with mutations in TP53, KRAS, BRAF, and other drivers potentially modulating this dependence. Lines with wild-type TP53 or specific oncogenic drivers might be less sensitive.

features.basis: Observed pattern: most sensitive lines have TP53 mutations, while many resistant lines lack them or have other mutations.
Observed pattern: KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines (T3M4, GSU, CL11) but also in some resistant lines, suggesting context-dependent effect.
Observed pattern: BRAF mutations in sensitive lines (HEC265, UACC62, K029AX) but also in resistant lines (LOXIMVI, IGR37), indicating possible sensitization in certain backgrounds.
Observed pattern: NRAS mutations in sensitive lines (IPC298, KU1919) but not in resistant lines shown.
Observed pattern: CDKN2A mutations in sensitive lines (SNU1214, IPC298, K029AX) but also in resistant MHHES1.
Observed pattern: PTEN mutations in several resistant lines (KALS1, ZR751, 786O) and in sensitive HEC265 and UACC62, suggesting possible protective role in some contexts.
Observed pattern: NF1 mutations in resistant lines (LOXIMVI, KALS1, S117) and in sensitive BICR6 and FTC133, indicating context-dependent effect.
Observed pattern: EGFR mutations in resistant lines (HCC4006, NCIH1437) and in sensitive KYSE270 and NCIH1650, suggesting possible protective role in lung context.
Mechanism: TAK-715 targets p38 MAPK (MAPK14); higher expression may increase dependence on p38 signaling for survival.
Mechanism: TAK-715 cross-reacts with casein kinase 1δ (CSNK1D), inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling; expression may predict sensitivity.
Mechanism: TAK-715 cross-reacts with casein kinase 1ε (CSNK1E), inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling; expression may predict sensitivity.
Mechanism: Mutations in CTNNB1 can activate Wnt/β-catenin signaling independently of CK1, potentially reducing sensitivity to TAK-715's CK1 inhibition; observed in resistant KE39.
